newsitem.title: USA: Judiciary panel praises Justice nominee Holder.
newsitem.headline: Judiciary panel praises Justice nominee Holder.

text.p: Members of the Senate Judiciary Committee Friday heaped bipartisan praise on Eric Holder at his confirmation hearings for the second-ranking position in the U.S. Department of Justice.

The panel did not vote on the nomination but praised Holder, a 46-year-old federal prosecutor who has supervised cases against international terrorists, drug kingpins, corrupt public officials and an attempted presidential assassin.

They also lauded Holder, who would be the first black deputy attorney general, for his community service. Among other things, he has long been involved in a mentoring organisation called Concerned Black Men and his office "adopted" an inner city school.

"I'll do my best to be one of the best friends you have on Capitol Hill," said committee Chairman Sen. Orrin Hatch, a Utah Republican. Senior committee Democrat Patrick Leahy of Vermont said Holder had the qualities that make "the difference between a prosecutor and a great prosecutor."
Clinton nominated Holder in March to fill one of several top jobs at Justice that have been empty for months. He announced his choices for several other senior Justice posts in the last few days.

Holder is the U.S. attorney for Washington, the city's top prosecutor for federal crimes. He has also worked in the Justice Department's elite Public Integrity Section, handling corruption cases, and in 1988 President Ronald Reagan named him a judge on D.C. Superior court, which handles local cases.

Republicans on the panel asked him some tough questions about the death penalty, juvenile crime, the Whitewater scandal and whether he agreed with Attorney General Janet Reno's decision not to seek an independent counsel to probe aspects of the campaign finance scandal.
But Hatch, almost apologetically, said the questions were being posed to get the answer "on the record" and were not likely to derail the nomination.

Sen. Arlen Specter, a Pennsylvania Republican, did say he would oppose further action on the nomination until Reno replies to some letters senators have sent her. Committee staff said they expect the nomination to move swiftly.
